Trading Sessions Example

CDate and the systime.h functions applied to US stock market sessions, holidays and trading days.

Contents

Running It
Sample Output
Source

What It Shows

CDate is the 4-byte date to store in records; it parses and prints M/D/YYYY and compares dates but does no calendar arithmetic, so the program adds day-of-week, next-day and trading-day math with std::tm and mktime(). The systime.h functions format the time stamps.

The rules, all in US Eastern time: pre-market 4:00 to 9:30, regular 9:30 to 16:00, post-market 16:00 to 20:00, closed otherwise and on weekends and the 2026 NYSE holidays. On the two early close days the regular session ends at 13:00 and the post-market at 17:00. 9:30 belongs to the regular session and 16:00 to the post-market.

It prints the session for sample times (each checked), the trading days in November 2026, the next trading day after some dates, and the current session in New York (POSIX systems, through the TZ setting).

Running It

trading_sessions                       # samples, a month and now
trading_sessions 11/27/2026 13:05      # one date and time (ET)
